title: On the chromatic profile for tripartite graphs and beyond
summary: Let $H$ be a graph and let $δ_χ(H,r)$ denote the infimum of $c$ such that every $H$-free graph with minimum degree at least $cn$ is $r$-colorable. The \textit{chromatic profile} of $H$ is defined to be the values of $δ_χ(H,r)$ as $r$ varies. Erdős and Simonovits described this graph parameter as ``too complicated", and Allen, Böttcher, Griffiths, Kohayakawa, and Morris posed its determination for every graph $H$ as an open problem \cite[Problem~45]{ABGKM2013}, emphasizing its expected difficulty.
